name: Is there a best time of year to renovate an older home in San Diego?

mainEntity.name: Is there a best time of year to renovate an older home in San Diego?

acceptedAnswer.text: Plan for weather and seasonal exposure even in Southern California, especially when roofs, windows, exterior walls, drainage, or coastal finishes are opened. Context: an older home may have less forgiving water-management details, so temporary protection and sequencing matter when exterior work is underway. Key factors: rainy-season timing, exposed openings, roof condition, site drainage, material storage, and interior protection. Practical guidance: ask how the contractor will protect the home if conditions change and which exterior tasks should be completed first. Do not leave vulnerable assemblies open without a documented temporary-protection plan. This is particularly relevant for coastal properties and homes with prior moisture damage.
acceptedAnswer.description: Indoor work can often proceed year-round, but projects that open roofs, windows, stucco, or exterior walls need careful weather planning. Ask about temporary protection, drainage, material storage, and sequencing, especially for older coastal homes or properties with moisture problems.
